blocks: ## Why this matters لِمَاذَا نُتْقِنُ الْمُضَارِعَ؟
Present forms power routines, descriptions, opinions, general facts and many future and modal structures.
### Core
Use the main singular forms and recognise أ، ت، ي، ن.
### Develop
Produce dual, masculine plural and feminine plural forms.
### Stretch
Explain context-dependent meaning and apply weak-verb changes.
[callout] Communication target: Respond accurately about what people do, are doing and regularly experience.
## Diagnostic start
Identify what the front and end of each verb tell you.
## The أ، ت، ي، ن prefix family
Present conjugation begins at the front of the verb.

TABLE: Prefix | Core person | Example // أَـ | أَنَا | أَكْتُبُ // نَـ | نَحْنُ | نَكْتُبُ // يَـ | هُوَ and many third-person forms | يَكْتُبُ // تَـ | أَنْتَ, هِيَ and several dual/plural forms | تَكْتُبُ
[callout] تَكْتُبُ is ambiguous without context: it can mean “you m.s. write” or “she writes”. The surrounding pronoun, noun or conversation resolves the subject.
## The complete present paradigm
The same suffix families recur across many verbs.

TABLE: Pronoun | Present form of كَتَبَ / يَكْتُبُ // أَنَا | أَكْتُبُ // نَحْنُ | نَكْتُبُ // أَنْتَ | تَكْتُبُ // أَنْتِ | تَكْتُبِينَ // أَنْتُمَا | تَكْتُبَانِ // أَنْتُمْ | تَكْتُبُونَ // أَنْتُنَّ | تَكْتُبْنَ // هُوَ | يَكْتُبُ // هِيَ | تَكْتُبُ // هُمَا (m.) | يَكْتُبَانِ // هُمَا (f.) | تَكْتُبَانِ // هُمْ | يَكْتُبُونَ // هُنَّ | يَكْتُبْنَ
[callout] Prefix + suffix: Dual, masculine plural, feminine singular addressee and feminine plural forms need information at both ends.
## Habit, current action and general truth
Time words and communicative context determine the intended time frame.

TABLE: Meaning | Arabic model | Context clue // habit | أَقْرَأُ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ. | كُلَّ يَوْمٍ // current action | أَقْرَأُ الآنَ. | الآنَ // general fact | تَدُورُ الْأَرْضُ حَوْلَ الشَّمْسِ. | general knowledge // arranged future | أُسَافِرُ غَدًا. | غَدًا; often strengthened with سـ
[callout/warning] Arabic present is not identical to one English tense. It can correspond to “I write”, “I am writing” or an arranged “I travel tomorrow”, depending on context.
## Present forms of weak verbs
The person framework remains stable while the weak stem adapts.

TABLE: Verb family | Past / present | Forms to notice // sound | كَتَبَ / يَكْتُبُ | أَكْتُبُ، تَكْتُبِينَ، يَكْتُبُونَ // hollow | قَالَ / يَقُولُ | أَقُولُ، تَقُولِينَ، يَقُولُونَ // initial weak | وَصَلَ / يَصِلُ | أَصِلُ، تَصِلِينَ، يَصِلُونَ // final weak y | مَشَى / يَمْشِي | أَمْشِي، تَمْشِينَ، يَمْشُونَ // final weak w | دَعَا / يَدْعُو | أَدْعُو، تَدْعِينَ، يَدْعُونَ
[callout] Watch plural spellings: يَمْشُونَ and يَدْعُونَ do not preserve every visible letter of the singular stem in the same way.
## Present-tense misconception clinic
A useful correction explains the form, not only the answer.
### Prefix ambiguity
✗ هِيَ يَكْتُبُ
✓ هِيَ تَكْتُبُ
Feminine third-person singular uses تـ.
### Feminine addressee
✗ أَنْتِ تَكْتُبُ
✓ أَنْتِ تَكْتُبِينَ
Add ـين for you feminine singular.
### Feminine plural
✗ هُنَّ تَكْتُبْنَ
✓ هُنَّ يَكْتُبْنَ
Third-person feminine plural begins with يـ.
### English tense transfer
✗ أَقْرَأُ = I am reading only
✓ أَقْرَأُ = I read / I am reading, according to context
Arabic present covers more than one English present construction.
## Replayable person builder
Build complete present forms rapidly.
## Apply the grammar across skills
Grammar becomes useful when it helps you understand and communicate.
### 📖 Reading workshop
Read a school profile and use prefixes/suffixes to identify speakers, addressees and reported people.
### 🎧 Listening workshop
Listen for minimal contrasts such as تَكْتُبُ / تَكْتُبِينَ / يَكْتُبُونَ / يَكْتُبْنَ.
### 🗣️ Speaking workshop
Give a one-minute routine answer, then change the subject from “I” to “we” and from a male friend to a female friend.
### 🛠️ Editing workshop
Correct present forms with wrong prefixes, missing plural endings and over-literal English tense interpretations.
### ✍️ Integrated production task
Write 120–140 words about your routine, current priorities and one general fact about your school or community. Use at least eight present verbs and six different persons.
[callout] Model: أَسْتَيْقِظُ مُبَكِّرًا، وَتَسْتَيْقِظُ أُخْتِي بَعْدِي. نَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ مَعًا، وَيَدْرُسُ أَصْدِقَائِي مَوَادَّ مُخْتَلِفَةً.
[callout] Success checklist: Include a habit, a current action, a general fact, one hollow verb, one final-weak verb and a feminine plural or dual form.
Save and mark complete Clear
Plan the verb changes as a timeline, root map or sentence flowchart. Label each form in Arabic.
Colour-code prefixes and box suffixes. Add the time/context clue beside each sentence.
## Final mastery check
Build the complete present form from the subject.
### Lesson mastery summary
- use the أ، ت، ي، ن prefixes accurately;
- add present suffixes for feminine, dual and plural persons;
- interpret habitual and current meanings from context;
- conjugate common weak verbs in the present.
Return in 3–7 days and repeat the final check without reviewing first. Retrieval, not recognition alone, builds secure verb control.
